title: A leaderboard
description:
Players are records such as `{ name = "Ada", score = 120 }`. Fill in:

```lua-norun
rank(players)           -- sorts the list in place: highest score first, equal scores by name (A to Z),
                        -- and returns the same table
top(players, n)         -- a NEW list of the names of the n best players (fewer if there are not n)
sorted_keys(t)          -- the keys of any table whose keys are strings, as a sorted list
leaderboard(players)    -- one string: "1. Ada 120" lines joined with "\n", in ranked order
```
hints: A comparison for two keys: `if a.score ~= b.score then return a.score > b.score end return a.name < b.name`.
rules: Use table.sort with a comparison function.
Build the leaderboard text with table.concat.
unitTests:
local function sample()
    return {
        { name = "Linus", score = 80 },
        { name = "Ada", score = 120 },
        { name = "Grace", score = 95 },
        { name = "Alan", score = 95 },
    }
end

test("rank sorts in place", function()
    local players = sample()
    local result = rank(players)
    check(result == players, "rank returns the same table it sorted")
    check_eq(players[1].name, "Ada")
    check_eq(players[2].name, "Alan")
    check_eq(players[3].name, "Grace")
    check_eq(players[4].name, "Linus")
end)

test("top n", function()
    check_eq(top(sample(), 2), { "Ada", "Alan" })
    check_eq(top(sample(), 10), { "Ada", "Alan", "Grace", "Linus" })
    check_eq(top({}, 3), {})
end)

test("sorted keys", function()
    check_eq(sorted_keys({ pear = 1, apple = 2, fig = 3 }), { "apple", "fig", "pear" })
    check_eq(sorted_keys({}), {})
end)

test("the leaderboard text", function()
    check_eq(leaderboard(sample()), "1. Ada 120\n2. Alan 95\n3. Grace 95\n4. Linus 80")
    check_eq(leaderboard({}), "")
end)
